answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching primary vendors (memory_c2) carries a documented SLA-miss risk that could break the line under zero slack—unacceptable given the 'no increased delivery risk' objective. Memory_c4 shows renegotiating at renewal has historically recovered real margin and improved payment terms without altering scope or stability, directly addressing the 18% spend-cut mandate while preserving the integration continuity seen in memory_c1. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is valuable for resilience but doesn't itself solve the imminent contract expiration or cost mandate this cycle, and multi-year commitment (memory_c6) requires more analysis time than the 14-day window allows. I verified c4 and c2 specifically to confirm the negotiation upside and the switching downside before committing capacity to this single decision.
